sourceInformation.source: Auto Racing (Mattel Intellivision, 1980; APh / Larry Zwick)
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade circuit racing and pursuit competition
sourceInformation.perspective: Stable north-up overhead; native 80-degree top-down view
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), AI Hub protocol 1 / session client 1.4.0 (35a1047), WebRTC data channels; Node 24 build tools
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded code-drawn retro pixel countryside; native shapes, materials, roads, cars and depth-sorted props
sourceInformation.animation: Native shape groups, tweens, particles and Humanoid rigs; steering wheels, suspension, driver lean, pit-crew reactions, windmill sails, skids, dust, impact stars and splash rings.
sourceInformation.audio: Web Audio synthesized engine, slip, surfaces, cues and gibberish crew; original procedural title/driving/finish music, initial music gain 0.10; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: Shared-world host-authoritative AI Hub duels; standalone manual offer/answer WebRTC with matched motors; couch shared-keyboard, pad+keyboard and two-pad duels; AI opponent. Two local browser contexts and the official Hub harness are the permitted stand-ins. Cross-NAT internet, TURN and real remote-device connectivity: unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless/state checks behind node tools/test.mjs; input-driven full tour, 2/5-lap trials, all course/car laps, controller/touch stand-ins, audio offline/analyser checks, real local WebRTC channels, and official Hub scenarios with 150 ms latency / 50 ms jitter / 5% loss; no FPS target.
sourceInformation.research: Original Mattel instructions and corrected Blue Sky Rangers history, scanned manual illustrations, archival gameplay still, pinned engine/Hub contracts, official WebRTC guidance. Original music and exact course dimensions unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Ubuntu Linux on WSL2

testingFeedback: 13 unique issues caught and fixed; details and confirming checks are recorded in docs/issues.md.
5 critical issues: a boot syntax error, blocked grand-course progress, dropped same-tick finish, unbounded direct disconnect, and shared-keyboard seat aliases.
The complete input-driven 11-stop tour and all 25 course/car legal-lap combinations; together they exposed progress and passport failures that smoke tests missed.
The cold-boot smoke check was useful but too narrow to reveal later route, menu, input, and connection failures.
engineFeedback: Native code-drawn shapes, E.Car, deterministic 120 Hz headless advance, and the controller-aware E.Shell made a coherent foundation.
The car brake could reverse from rest, and restoring a solo input preset after seat assignment reintroduced both players’ arrow aliases. Explicit adapters and tests resolved both.
A directed-gate route tracker and one host-authoritative pursuit simulation reused by local, WebRTC and Hub play.
Integrating native Shell pause/focus with live online menus and a match clock that works in an actorless server copy.
No upstream engine modifications. Game adapters use reverse:0, freeze grids, preserve analog intents, arbitrate pursuit incidents, and separate coincident cars before native contact.
Add a native directed-gate race-progress helper that handles shared roads, recovery anchors and ordered crossings.
promptFeedback: The source identity, exact hand-in naming, single-file requirement, and explicit hardware stand-ins made the delivery concrete.
PLAN.md specifies ultra effort while TASK.md specifies max. TASK.md was used for filenames and model metadata.
Completing controller/touch UX, legal route tracking and three multiplayer paths around one consistent simulation.
Keep a short mandatory acceptance checklist beside the delivery contract, with implementation suggestions and pacing targets separate.

aiHub.name: Auto Motley Motor
aiHub.tagline: Little cars. Lovely roads. Big mistakes.
aiHub.description: Brake before the bend and take the scenic line through five connected county circuits. Race the clock, trade pursuit points with a friend, or find the old airfield.
aiHub.controls: A/D or arrows steer; S/Down/Space brake; hold R recover; Enter confirm; Esc pause. Pad: left stick, L2 brake, Triangle recover, Options menu. Touch: drag left to steer, hold right to brake.
